newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones first half sales fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones first half sales fall.

text.p: Upmarket retail group David Jones Ltd said on Tuesday that sales in the 26 weeks ended January 25 this year fell one percent to A$782.6 million from A$790.3 million a year ago.
The retailer also said sales in the second quarter had shown a substantial improvement over the 1996/97 first quarter.
"Sales in the second quarter showed a substantial improvement over the first quarter as a result of the good trading in January, particularly during Clearance," the company said.
"January Sales were significantly above the same month last year, improving the year to date figures from a negative 2.9 percent variance as at the end of December," it said.
"The sales improvement in January will have a marginally positive impact on the level of the first half profit previously forecast," David Jones said.
The company said sales from the David Jones department stores in the latest 26 weeks rose 1.3 percent to A$718.5 million, but dropped 2.9 percent of a like-for-like basis.
Sales at the three remaining John Martin stores based in South Australia fell 20.8 percent in the latest half year to A$64.1 million.
Total first half sales fell 4.7 percent on a like-for-like basis.
In the latest second quarter, total sales rose by 0.3 percent to A$472.1 million from A$470.5 million a year ago, but fell 2.9 percent of a like-for-like basis.
First quarter sales fell 2.9 percent to A$310.5 million from A$319.8 million a year ago, and dropped by 7.1 percent on a like-for-like basis.
